targets.title: Augmented-reality surgical system using depth sensing
System and method for fault identification, logging, and remediation
Method for training a driving related object detector
Method and apparatus for additive manufacturing with shared components
Air knife assembly for additive manufacturing

method: Targets: 10 US patents with priority dates from 2019 on, each citing a patent in our graveyard sample, each with 3 to 30 examiner-cited US references.
Input: title, abstract and first independent claim only. The agent never sees the citation list.
Search space: documents with a priority date before the target's, excluding the target and its family.

Corpus: 36,004 US documents. 35,069 come from our sample's citation neighborhood (cached pages and the documents they cite or are cited by; target pages excluded). The other 935 are the targets' full citation tables, examiner and applicant references alike, pooled in as title-only rows like most of the corpus. This is a pooled benchmark, not a search of every US patent.
Ground truth: references marked as examiner-cited on the patent record, US documents with an earlier priority date than the target.
Comparison: one keyword search built from the description's most frequent terms, same corpus, same cutoffs.
An earlier run on the same targets, before we fixed how the search tool reads boolean queries (it had dropped phrases and ANDs), found 13 of 83 (16%). Prompts were not changed between runs.
